articles.name: Configuring outbound queue selection in Contact Center
articles.title: Configuring outbound queue selection in Contact Center
articles.body:
Outbound queue selection lets agents choose the queue from which they place an outbound call. The selected queue determines the phone number displayed to the recipient and the Amazon Connect flow that handles the call.

What's my plan?
Add-on Contact Center

Summary: ◀▼

You can let agents choose an outbound queue for calls, which controls the caller ID shown to recipients and the flow that handles the call. You can allow access to all queues or only queues tied to the agent’s routing profile. This helps you manage outbound call routing and queue selection, but calls from queues without an outbound number will fail.

Location: Contact Center > Routing > Outbound calls.

Outbound queue selection lets agents choose the queue from which they place an outbound call. The selected queue determines the phone number displayed to the recipient and the Amazon Connect flow that handles the call.

For information about configuring routing profiles and their queues, see Updating Amazon Connect routing profiles for Contact Center. For the agent procedure, see Selecting the outbound queue for a call.

To turn on outbound queue selection

  1. In Contact Center, click Routing > Outbound calls.

  2. Select Allow agents to select an outbound queue.
  3. Select the queues that agents can access:
    • All queues: Agents can place a call from any queue, regardless of their Amazon Connect routing profile.
    • All queues associated with the agent's routing profile: Agents can place a call only from queues associated with their Amazon Connect routing profile.
Note: Queues appear to agents even if they don't have an outbound number. Calls placed using those queues fail.

articles.name: Updating Amazon Connect routing profiles for Contact Center
articles.title: Updating Amazon Connect routing profiles for Contact Center
articles.body:
A routing profile in Amazon Connect defines the queues that agents can handle, the priority and delay for each queue, and the maximum number of simultaneous contacts. It also sets the default outbound queue for agent-initiated calls.

What's my plan?
Add-on Contact Center

Summary: ◀▼

You can update an Amazon Connect routing profile to control which queues agents handle, set queue priority and delay, and limit concurrent contacts. This helps you manage agent capacity and set the default outbound queue for agent-initiated calls. If you turn on outbound queue selection, agents can choose an outbound queue for calls.

A routing profile in Amazon Connect defines the queues that agents can handle, the priority and delay for each queue, and the maximum number of simultaneous contacts. It also sets the default outbound queue for agent-initiated calls.

Each agent has one routing profile. To let agents choose an outbound queue, turn on outbound queue selection in Contact Center. For more information, see Configuring outbound queue selection in Contact Center.

For more information about creating routing profiles and linking queues to agents, see Create a routing profile in Amazon Connect to link queues to agents in the AWS documentation.

To update a routing profile

  1. In Amazon Connect, click Users > Routing profiles.
  2. Click the routing profile you want to edit.
  3. Update the channels, queues, and concurrency settings as needed.

  4. Click Save.

articles.name: Announcing WhatsApp usernames in the Agent Workspace
articles.title: Announcing WhatsApp usernames in the Agent Workspace
articles.body:
We’re happy to announce that you can now view WhatsApp usernames in the Agent Workspace.

This article includes the following sections:

  • What is changing?
  • Why is Zendesk making this change?
  • What do I need to do?

What is changing?

When WhatsApp provides a username, it appears in the customer profile in the Agent Workspace. The WhatsApp phone number also appears when it is available.

This gives agents visibility into WhatsApp-specific customer information, including when a customer’s phone number is not shared.

Why is Zendesk making this change?

WhatsApp is introducing usernames as an additional way for people to identify themselves when contacting businesses. Because a customer’s phone number may not always be shared, displaying the WhatsApp username helps agents recognize and distinguish customers during support interactions.

WhatsApp usernames and phone numbers are provided by Meta. Usernames may change over time, so they are displayed as profile information rather than as a permanent customer identity. Agents cannot edit either value.

What do I need to do?

No action is required to enable this change. WhatsApp usernames and phone numbers appear automatically in the customer profile when they are provided by Meta.

Keep the following in mind:

  • If Meta does not provide a username or phone number, the corresponding field remains blank.
  • Agents cannot edit WhatsApp usernames or phone numbers received from Meta.
  • Once a WhatsApp phone number is displayed in the customer profile, Zendesk does not remove it.
  • If a customer’s phone number is available when they contact you through WhatsApp, Zendesk also populates the standard phone number field if it is empty.

Admins may want to update internal guidance and inform agents about the new WhatsApp profile information.

If you have feedback or questions related to this announcement, visit our community forum where we collect and manage customer product feedback. For general assistance with your Zendesk products, contact Zendesk Customer Support.

articles.name: Error: Zendesk Support could not be loaded due to an error
articles.title: Error: Zendesk Support could not be loaded due to an error
articles.body:
Issue symptoms

When I try to sign in to Zendesk, I see the error: Zendesk Support could not be loaded due to an error.

In the browser console and network logs, I may see 5xx errors.

Resolution steps

Antivirus or VPN tools can block access to required Zendesk resources and cause this error. Confirm whether affected agents still see the error when they connect from a device that doesn’t use these tools.

If users still have issues, contact Zendesk Customer Support and include an HTTP Archive (HAR) file from one affected user.

Why do I see "Zendesk Support could not be loaded due to an error"? How do I fix "Zendesk Support could not be loaded due to an error" when signing in? What causes "Zendesk Support could not be loaded due to an error"?

Antivirus or VPN tools can block access to required Zendesk resources and cause 5xx errors in browser console and network logs.

To resolve this error, follow these steps:

  1. Connect to your Zendesk help desk or ticketing system from a device that does not use VPN or antivirus tools.
  2. Check if the error disappears.
  3. If you still see the error, contact Zendesk Customer Support.
  4. Provide an HTTP Archive (HAR) file from an affected support person or agent.

articles.name: Service Incident - September 17, 2026 - Voice | Elevated Average Active Sessions on shard cluster 20.7 / sharddb-20-07 in Pod 20
articles.title: Service Incident - September 17, 2026 - Voice | Elevated Average Active Sessions on shard cluster 20.7 / sharddb-20-07 in Pod 20
articles.body:
Summary

Between 14:26 UTC and 17:40 UTC on 17 September 2026, Voice customers on Pod 20 experienced an issue that caused some agents to remain in wrap-up mode after calls. Affected agents were not offered new incoming calls, which could delay inbound call handling.

Timeline

September 17, 2026 16:53 UTC | September 17, 2026 9:53 AM PT

We are aware of an issue affecting Voice on Pod 20 that is causing agents to experience difficulties leaving wrap-up mode. We are also seeing some call recordings not appended to tickets as expected. We are investigating and will provide further information when we have a substantive update to share. In the meantime, we recommend trying to manually click "finish wrap-up" (don't wait for the auto-timeout), and in case "finish wrap-up" doesn't respond, toggle Voice availability Off then On. Please let us know if the issue persists after attempting the workaround. Thank you for your patience in the meantime.

September 17, 2026 18:25 UTC | September 17, 2026 11:25 AM PT

Our team has addressed the underlying cause of the issue that prevented some agents from exiting wrap-up mode after a Voice call.  Agents ending a call should see wrap-up, and all relevant agent availability functions are back to normal. Thank you for your patience while we recovered from this incident.

Root Cause Analysis

This incident was caused by a high volume of duplicate agent availability updates generated by a single Voice session. Because the service did not adequately prevent duplicate requests or limit repeated updates from an individual agent, the traffic overwhelmed shared processing capacity on Pod 20 and delayed lower-priority work.

Resolution

To resolve the issue, we temporarily disabled the affected account’s embedded calling feature to stop further repeated availability updates. We then allowed pending work to be processed and re-enabled the feature after system performance had stabilized.

Remediation Items

  1. Introduce limits on how frequently an individual user can submit availability updates.
  2. Add a controlled way to immediately pause embedded calling updates when abnormal activity is detected.
  3. Separate availability checks from the primary system responsible for saving updates, reducing pressure on critical services.
  4. Apply stricter safeguards to prevent excessive or repeated availability changes from being processed.
  5. Prioritize the work required to return agents to an available state after a call, reducing the likelihood of delayed incoming call handling.

FOR MORE INFORMATION

For current system status information about Zendesk and specific impacts to your account, visit our system status page. If you have additional questions about this incident, contact Zendesk customer support.

articles.name: I am trying to deploy to far more than 50 organizations with AI agents
articles.title: I am trying to deploy to far more than 50 organizations with AI agents
articles.body:
Issue symptoms

I am trying to deploy to far more than 50 organizations with AI agents. My company provides customer support for other organizations. Because of this, I use 1 web crawler per organization that I support.

The problem is there is a limit of 50 web crawlers for each AI agent. I am trying to deploy to far more than 50 organizations, but we are unable to import any knowledge from said organizations due to the limit on web crawlers. Do you have advice on a workaround or re-architecting this build with best practices?

Resolution steps

Firstly, the web crawler does not have a limit for each AI agent, but for each Zendesk account.

  • Consider reaching out to your sales team at Zendesk to ask for an alternative.

In addition, if your team has developer and engineering resources, you may be interested to make use of the Federated Search API concept and these 2 methods:

  • The Web crawler lets your team implement federated search in your help center without developer resources. Set up multiple crawlers in your help center search settings to crawl and index different content in the same or different websites.
  • The Federated Search API allows developers to build custom integrations and ingest external content records into your Zendesk search indexes. This API requires your developers to build and maintain a middleware layer and integrate the site that hosts the external content with the help center. External records ingested through the Federated Search API refresh based on your configuration, whereas web crawlers run based on your selected refresh schedule (daily, weekly, monthly, or never) or can be triggered manually.

articles.name: Knowledge sources don't pull CSV knowledge I uploaded
articles.title: Knowledge sources don't pull CSV knowledge I uploaded
articles.body:
Issue symptoms

I am using CSV knowledge and AI agents - Advanced (legacy). After installing the CSV Knowledge Importer, I can't get the AI Agent to pull from my CSV knowledge. No matter what question I am asking the AI agents for information from the CSV knowledge source, my bot simply goes to the default reply.

This is what I've done:

  • I have installed and added the CSV knowledge importer.
  • I have ensured the CSV knowledge is added as a knowledge source in AI Agents.
  • I then tried to ask the bot a very simple question from something I knew was in the CSV knowledge source.

Root cause

The Knowledge Reply use case may be restricted to articles from a Recommendation search rule.

Resolution steps

To solve this issue:

  1. Remove any Recommendation search restriction from your use case
  2. Ensure your Intent shows Generative replies > Response generated
  3. Publish your updated configuration
  4. Refresh the page or clear your cache and cookies, and the Knowledge sources should return replies

articles.name: Service Incident - September 16, 2026 - Support | Multiple Pods - Custom ticket status are deactivated and unable to reactivate issue
articles.title: Service Incident - September 16, 2026 - Support | Multiple Pods - Custom ticket status are deactivated and unable to reactivate issue
articles.body:
Summary

On September 16, 2026, from 09:00 UTC to 12:20 UTC, Support customers on multiple pods experienced an issue that caused custom ticket statuses to appear inactive or become unavailable. As a result, agents were unable to use or reactivate these statuses, disrupting routine ticket updates, macro execution, and related workflows until service was restored.

Timeline

September 16, 2026 11:14 UTC | September 16, 2026 4:14 AM PT

We are aware of an issue affecting custom ticket statuses. Some customers may see statuses marked as inactive and be unable to restore them, while other statuses may not appear at all. Our engineering team has identified the cause and is actively working to resolve the issue. We apologize for the disruption and will provide another update as soon as more information is available.

September 16, 2026 11:32 UTC | September 16, 2026 4:32 AM PT

We have deployed a fix for the issue affecting custom ticket statuses. Please check whether your statuses are now visible and can be managed as expected. If you still see missing or inactive statuses, please reply to let us know. We will be happy to continue investigating with you. We apologize for the disruption and appreciate your help in confirming the resolution.

September 16, 2026 12:13 UTC | September 16, 2026 5:13 AM PT

Our engineering team is continuing to roll out the fix for the custom ticket status issue to the remaining affected service environments. We appreciate your patience while this work is completed and will provide further updates as they become available.

September 16, 2026 12:41 UTC | September 16, 2026 5:41 AM PT

Our engineering teams have completed deployment of the fix. Please verify whether custom ticket statuses are now displaying and functioning as expected. If the issue persists, please clear your browser cache and cookies, then check the ticket statuses again using a private or incognito browser window. If the issue continues after these steps, please contact us so we can provide further assistance.

September 16, 2026 14:18 UTC | September 16, 2026 7:18 AM PT

We are happy to report that the issue affecting custom ticket statuses has been resolved. Thank you for your patience during our investigation.

Root Cause Analysis

This incident was caused by a production code change that removed a required setting used to determine whether custom ticket statuses were enabled. As a result, the system treated the feature as unavailable, causing custom ticket statuses to appear inactive or missing for affected customers.

Resolution

To resolve the issue, we halted the affected deployment and reverted the change that removed the required custom ticket status capability. We then performed controlled recovery actions to restore all affected Classic environments to the expected software version.

Remediation Items

  1. Add checks before and after updates to confirm custom ticket statuses continue working as expected.
  2. Improve the process for reversing updates so that service can be restored more reliably if an issue occurs.
  3. Make feature availability more consistent when product changes are introduced.
  4. Add additional safeguards to protect customer-facing features from being unintentionally affected by updates.
  5. Improve and standardize how service updates are published, ensuring communications are timely and consistent.

FOR MORE INFORMATION

For current system status information about Zendesk and specific impacts to your account, visit our system status page. If you have additional questions about this incident, contact Zendesk customer support.

articles.name: Announcing Microsoft Teams notifications for AI-powered Insights in real-time monitoring (EAP)
articles.title: Announcing Microsoft Teams notifications for AI-powered Insights in real-time monitoring (EAP)
articles.body:
We're adding Microsoft Teams notifications for customers using the Open EAP for AI-powered Insights and real-time monitoring dashboards. alongside the existing Slack and email notifications.

This announcement includes the following topics:

  • What is changing?
  • Why is Zendesk making this change?
  • What do I need to do?

What is changing?

This update adds Microsoft Teams as a notification channel, so any anomaly notifications can be notified over your preferred Microsoft Teams channels.

Why is Zendesk making this change?

Support teams that use Microsoft Teams as their primary collaboration channel can now receive anomaly notifications directly where they do their work. Microsoft Teams works alongside Slack and email, giving teams the flexibility to choose the notification channels that best fit their workflow.

What do I need to do?

If you are participating in the Open EAP, Microsoft Teams notifications are available for you to configure. See Viewing AI-powered insights in the real-time monitoring dashboards.

If you are not yet participating in the Open EAP and would like to join, follow these instructions.

If you have feedback or questions about this announcement, visit our community forum, where we collect and manage customer product feedback. For general assistance with your Zendesk products, contact Zendesk Customer Support.

articles.name: Release notes through 2026-09-25
articles.title: Release notes through 2026-09-25
articles.body:
See the What's New section for an overview of last month's releases.

This week's release notes include:

  • AI Agents
  • Knowledge
  • Contact Center
  • Voice
  • Zendesk QA
  • Apps and integrations
  • Products with no updates this week

AI Agents

New:

Auto Assist Procedure Recommendations and Management

  • Admins can now search across their Copilot auto assist procedures within Knowledge admin. This update simplifies retrieval and management for accounts managing large numbers of procedures. See  Viewing and managing procedures for auto assist.
  • Zendesk is introducing draft mode and version control for Copilot auto assist procedures in Knowledge admin, allowing admins to safely create, test, and restore procedure updates without impacting live agent suggestions. See Creating procedures for auto assist and Viewing and managing procedures for auto assist.

Fixed:

Auto Assist Procedure Recommendations and Management

  • Procedure list filter translations. The "Status" label in the procedures filter bar is now translated for non-English locales.

Knowledge

New:

Editor

  • Removed the non-actionable "no changes" save alert shown when saving an article without changes.

Knowledge Graph

  • Three new Knowledge connectors are available: Helpjuice, WordPress, and ReadMe.

Fixed:

Editor

  • Excluded-terms settings stay usable beside Admin Copilot. The sidebar is now responsive while preserving pinned actions.
  • Guide and Support admins can manage Knowledge AI settings. Added access, navigation, and write authorization for Knowledge settings.
  • Help Center collaborator-label contrast. The label now meets WCAG contrast requirements.

Contact Center

New:

  • Contact Center Voicemail is now available with a reusable Amazon Connect voicemail flow, optional per-queue transcription, configurable routing and tags, a default 60-second recording duration that can be configured in the flow, and Zendesk ticket creation or linking. Customers should customize an organisation-owned copy of the managed template. A stack update is required to enable the feature. See Configuring voicemail in Contact Center.

Fixed:

Contact Center App

  • Adjusted how contact attributes are handled during After Contact Work (ACW) on outbound calls, targeting intermittent duplicated ticket reports. 
  • Increased the maximum results shown in queue dropdowns so longer lists no longer get cut off. 
  • Added logging of ZCOS capabilities (zcos_proxy, list_real_time_transcripts, oauth), profile creation flag, and Cognito login-skip state on agent initialization, to support faster diagnosis of environment-related issues.

Voice

New:

  • Now, when omnichannel routing is enabled and a call expires in the queue, a tag voice_expired_in_queue is automatically added to the ticket. This tag can be used to filter out tickets from calls that were neither answered nor abandoned. 

Fixed:

  • We resolved an issue where the message composer would lose focus after the call ended, disrupting the agent's typing.

Zendesk QA

New:

  • Audit logs: QA now records review, scorecard and workspace events in Zendesk Admin Center audit logs.
  • Reviews: Existing reviews remain editable after a scorecard category scale is reduced.
  • Disputes: Historical-review disputes can be created or accepted after the original scorecard is deactivated.

Apps and integrations

New:
  • Zoom Workforce Management (Support)
    • Zoom WFM opens from the Zendesk top bar with a compact agent experience built for Zendesk. Agents can view their schedule and handle time off, schedule change, and swap requests without leaving the agent workspace. If your account enables it, agents can also access the schedule offer board directly in Zendesk. Relevant Workforce Management alerts appear as native Zendesk notifications, helping agents stay informed in one place. Key features include viewing schedules in a compact top bar experience, submitting time off requests from Zendesk, managing schedule change and swap requests, accessing the schedule offer board when enabled for your account, and receiving relevant WFM alerts as native Zendesk notifications.
  • DataSpeak Agent Assist (Support)
    • DataSpeak helps organizations answer questions faster, guide agents with reliable knowledge, and keep every conversation consistent with their brand voice — without losing control of workflows or data. DataSpeak brings your AI assistant into Zendesk Agent Workspace so agents get help without leaving the ticket.  Once connected, agents can chat with your DataSpeak assistant in the ticket sidebar, new ticket sidebar, user sidebar, and nav bar; get ticket-aware answers with subject, status, requester details, and related context passed into the conversation; summarize tickets, search Help Center knowledge, and draft clearer replies without switching tools; resume or thread chats per ticket via secure conversation references; and optionally identify the signed-in Zendesk agent in DataSpeak 
  • Super Search (Support)
    • Search tickets, macros, triggers, automations and more—all in one workspace. Super Search brings tickets, users and organizations together with searchable catalogs of macros, triggers, automations and webhooks, helping you find records and explore the configuration behind your support workflows. Super Search combines record search, configuration catalogs and per-ticket audit evidence in a navigation-bar workspace. 
  • Access Controller (Support)
    • LaPlante Management built Access Controller to help Zendesk teams protect important values from accidental edits, simplify crowded workspaces, and replace scattered field-ID lists with readable access profiles. Create an All agents baseline; build reusable profiles for Groups, Roles, or individual Agents; set supported fields and tag editors to Editable, Read-only, or Hide; set ticket forms to Editable or Hide; control individual Type, Priority, and eligible custom dropdown choices; vary field and choice rules by ticket form, brand, assigned group, or new/existing state; inspect an agent's matching profiles and compare effective access before saving; duplicate profiles and apply confirmed bulk changes; and open web addresses from read-only fields in a new browser tab. 
  • Similar Tickets (Support)
    • Similar Tickets brings useful ticket history into the conversation an agent is already handling. It searches the current Zendesk account, ranks related conversations, and displays the strongest matches directly in the ticket sidebar. Agents can review how similar incidents, questions, and customer issues were handled without leaving the ticket or guessing which search terms to use. 
  • Dual Frame (Support)
    • Designed by LaPlante Management, Dual Frame brings shared website bookmarks and embedded tools into Zendesk. Give agents one organized menu for reference pages, tools and reporting links, with no iframe code to write. Place bookmarks in full navigation, beside tickets or in a top-menu pop-up. Reuse them across locations and tailor menus to agent groups. 
  • Change Management (Support)
    • Change Management adds an ITIL change practice to Zendesk Support, running on native Zendesk tickets, forms, triggers, and approvals. Changes move from draft through assessment, CAB approval, scheduling, implementation, and post-implementation review to closure, with required fields enforced at each step. Impact and likelihood score change risk against a rubric your administrators control. A change calendar, collision detection for overlapping windows, and configurable freeze periods show what else is scheduled before you commit.
  • Incident Management (Support)
    • Incident Management adds an ITIL incident practice to Zendesk Support, running on native Zendesk tickets, forms, triggers, and approvals. Impact and urgency set Zendesk priority automatically through a matrix your administrators control. Major incidents unlock declaration, communication, and running update fields, along with a list of linked child incidents and a one-click way to raise the remediation change. Recurring pattern detection spots repeat incidents and can open a problem record with those incidents already linked to it.
  • Request Management (Support)
    • Request Management adds a service request practice to Zendesk Support, running on native Zendesk tickets, forms, triggers, and approvals. Requests move from submission through approval and fulfillment to closure, capturing catalog item, justification, and due date. Approval is routed to a person or a group through Zendesk's own approvals, so the decision and who made it stay on the ticket record. Work cannot begin until the request is approved, and fulfillment notes are required before it can be marked fulfilled.
  • Problem Management (Support)
    • Problem Management adds an ITIL problem practice to Zendesk Support, running on native Zendesk tickets, forms, triggers, and approvals. Problems move from open through investigation and known error to resolution, capturing root cause, workaround, RCA method, and permanent fix. Linked incidents are gathered from both Zendesk relationship types, and a similar-incident search lets you attach related incidents in bulk. Resolving a problem resolves its open incidents and records on each one why it was closed.

Products with no updates this week

  • Admin Center
  • Support
  • Copilot
  • Analytics
  • Zendesk Workforce Management (WFM)
  • Mobile SDKs

articles.name: Pre-built connectors don't work with custom actions
articles.title: Pre-built connectors don't work with custom actions
articles.body:
Issue symptoms

With AI agents, prebuilt connectors don't work with custom actions. These are prebuilt third-party connectors, also called managed connectors. For example, connectors for Shopify and Salesforce.

Root cause

Prebuilt connectors cannot be selected as the authentication method for a custom action.

Resolution steps

The workaround is to create a custom connection for these connections instead.

articles.name: Troubleshooting automations
articles.title: Troubleshooting automations
articles.body:
Use this guide if your automation returns errors.

Step one: Compare the expected ticket event and your automation conditions

To understand the root cause of the error, compare the ticket events and the conditions of your automation:

  1. Open your automation
  2. Side-by-side, open the ticket you expect to see the automation run on
  3. From the ticket, click the Events icon. Review the events at the time you expected to see the automation run.
  4. Look at the conditions of your automation to understand what doesn’t match your ticket
  5. Typically, the automation may not run if there are too many conditions under 'Meet all of the following conditions' that are not met at the same time by the ticket. Make sure the logic reflects your ticket.
  6. In addition, if you have a time or hour condition, do not use 'Is', but instead use 'Greater than'
Note: Automations are for time-based actions. For example, create an automation if you want an action to happen hours after a ticket status has changed. For direct action without time constraints, use Triggers instead.

Step two: Ensure your automation doesn’t run in a loop

To avoid automation loops, create a nullifying tag condition and action:

  1. Below Meet all of the following conditions, include a Ticket: Tags | Contains none of the following tag_abc
  2. Replace tag_abc with the tag of your choice
  3. Under Perform these actions, add: Ticket: Add tags and the same exact tag you added above. For example tag_abc.

Step three: Verify the result

After you edit the automation:

  1. Create a test ticket
  2. Open the ticket events and ensure your automation runs as expected
  3. If something is off, return to step 1 to troubleshoot and correct the issue with the conditions of your automation

articles.name: Workflow recipe: Configuring asynchronous ticket escalations for messaging AI agents
articles.title: Workflow recipe: Configuring asynchronous ticket escalations for messaging AI agents
articles.body:
In a messaging AI agent, you can configure an asynchronous ticket escalation path that lets customers leave a message when your team is unavailable, so a human agent can follow up later instead of continuing the conversation in real time.

What's my plan?
All Suites Team, Growth, Professional, Enterprise, or Enterprise Plus
Support Team, Professional, or Enterprise

In a messaging AI agent, you can configure an asynchronous ticket escalation path that lets customers leave a message when your team is unavailable, so a human agent can follow up later instead of continuing the conversation in real time.

This style of escalation may also be referred to as an offline escalation, an out-of-hours (OOH) escalation, or a ticket escalation.

An asynchronous ticket escalation can also be achieved using the “Send an email” option of an Escalation block in a dialogue, the Create Ticket API, or the Create ticket action. However, this workflow recipe describes the recommended workflow for human agent follow-up when live messaging is unavailable and is compatible with the AI agent ticket experience.

This article contains the following topics:

  • Workflow goal
  • Creating a configured action to tag escalated conversations
  • Adding the configured action to your escalation dialogues and templates
  • Creating a ticket trigger to end the messaging session for tagged conversations
  • Verifying that asynchronous escalations are working correctly

Workflow goal

When a customer reaches out on a messaging channel during a time when your support team is unavailable, you want to escalate the customer’s request as a ticket in Zendesk Support so that one of your team members can respond during business hours.

Once configured, the workflow looks like this:

  1. The customer begins a conversation with your messaging AI agent.
  2. The AI agent is unable to resolve the customer’s request and the conversation needs to be escalated to a human agent, but it’s outside your business hours and your support team is unavailable.
  3. The conversation is escalated using the “Forward to agent” setting in an Escalation block of a dialogue, creating a ticket in Zendesk Support.
  4. A tag is added to the conversation that identifies it as an asynchronous escalation.
  5. The original messaging session is ended by a ticket trigger.

Before you begin

  • This recipe describes a basic setup. If your Zendesk account uses extensive customization or unique routing settings, the required steps may vary.
  • This recipe applies only to escalations that originate from dialogues in messaging AI agents. Escalations from generative procedures aren’t covered.
  • This recipe uses a conversation tag to identify asynchronous ticket escalations. You can customize your workflow to use other metadata, provided it’s available in messaging, supported by the AI agent, and can be evaluated as a ticket trigger condition.
  • It’s strongly recommended to test this workflow in a sandbox environment before making changes to your production environment.

Prerequisites

  • Create a messaging AI agent.
  • Identify every dialogue or template you currently have that includes an Escalation block used for an asynchronous escalation. This is typically done by pairing an Availability block with the Escalation block, but you may not always use the Availability block.
  • Choose a unique conversation tag, such as async_escalation. You’ll use the same tag in the configured action and the ticket trigger.
  • Turn on the end messaging session feature for agents.

Creating a configured action to tag escalated conversations

First, create a configured action that you can use to tag escalated conversations. You’ll use this tag as a condition in the ticket trigger you’ll create later.

To create the configured action

  1. In the AI agents workspace, select the AI agent you want to work with.
  2. Click Actions in the sidebar, then select Configured actions.
  3. Click Create configured action.
  4. In Name, enter a descriptive name, such as “Tag asynchronous escalations.”
  5. In Target, select Sunshine Conversations.
  6. In Task, select Add conversation tags.
  7. In Tags, enter your unique conversation tag, such as async_escalation, and click Add.
  8. Click Create.

The configured action is now available for use in your dialogues and templates.

Adding the configured action to your escalation dialogues and templates

Next, add the configured action you just created to any escalation dialogue or template that’s designed to present an option to customers when your human agents are unavailable. This adds a tag to escalated conversations that you can target with a ticket trigger.

To update the escalation reply

  1. Open the existing dialogue or template you want to add the configured action to.
  2. Select the appropriate Escalation block.

    For example, if you’re using the Availability block, select the Escalation block connected to the Closed branch.

  3. In the block, click the dropdown and select Forward to an agent.
  4. In the Details panel on the right, click the dropdown under Configured actions and select the configured action you created above (“Tag asynchronous escalations” in the example).

  5. Click Publish.

    Publishing makes the updated escalation available for testing and, if you’re working in your production environment, available to end users. Your previous escalation setup is still accessible through the version history, if necessary.

Escalations outside of your business hours are now forwarded to a human agent and have the specified tag applied to them.

Creating a ticket trigger to end the messaging session for tagged conversations

Finally, create a ticket trigger that ends the messaging session for any tagged conversations. This allows your support team to assist the customer at a later point through the escalated ticket, rather than as part of a real-time messaging conversation. For more information about what happens when a messaging session ends, see About ending messaging sessions.

Note: Make sure to test and review any ticket routing changes before publishing the trigger in your production environment.

To create the ticket trigger

  1. In Admin Center, click Objects and rules in the sidebar, then select Business rules > Triggers.
  2. On the triggers page, select the Ticket tab.
  3. Click Create trigger.
  4. In Trigger name, enter a descriptive name, such as “End messaging session for asynchronous escalations.”
  5. (Optional) In Description, enter details about what the trigger does.

    You can search for triggers by their description.

  6. In Trigger category, select AI agents.
  7. Under Meet ALL of the following conditions, click Add condition and add the following conditions:
    • Ticket > Tags | Contains at least one of the following | <your conversation tag>
    • Ticket > Channel | Is | Messaging

  8. Under Actions, click Add action and add the following action:
    • Ticket > Messaging session | End Session

      Important: Do not use Ticket > Set routing channel as an additional action in this trigger. For more information, see Ticket routing.
  9. Click Create trigger.

Verifying that asynchronous escalations are working correctly

After you’ve configured your asynchronous ticket escalation setup, you should test your workflow to ensure your configuration is working as you intend.

To verify asynchronous escalations

  1. Start a test conversation that meets your outside-of-business-hours condition.
  2. Follow the escalation path.
  3. In the Agent Workspace, open the resulting ticket.
  4. Confirm the following:
    • The ticket contains the conversation tag you created.
    • The ticket events show that the messaging session ended.
    • If the requester has an email address: The composer defaults to a public reply using email.
    • If the requester does not have an email address: The composer defaults to an internal note.

The ticket is ready for asynchronous handling.

articles.name: How do I avoid emails becoming suspended tickets?
articles.title: How do I avoid emails becoming suspended tickets?
articles.body:
Question

How do I avoid emails becoming suspended tickets? My email or web form tickets are missing or appear as suspended tickets or spam. How do I resolve this?

Answer

Suspended tickets have several potential causes and the correct way to address the issue depends on your account setup. To determine the correct way to resolve the issue, open one of the tickets within the Suspended tickets view and examine the listed cause of suspension.

One of the most common reasons for suspended tickets is when you have a web form set up to forward requests as emails using the same email listed as a support address. These tickets can show up as suspended tickets with the cause "Received from support address".

To resolve this, configure your email channel so that no potential mail loop can occur. Ensure the from: and reply-to: addresses on any email request list the intended end user instead of your support address. You can also use the API to configure a web form instead of an email forwarding method. For more information on how to resolve this, see:

  • Tickets created from my custom ticket form are suspended
  • What does the cause of suspension message “Received from support address” mean?

Best practices to avoid creating suspended tickets from email

Use one of the recommended methods to create a form to submit tickets, instead of any setup that lets a web form forward requests with an email already listed as one of your support addresses.

Check your external email server forwarding setup to ensure it aligns with the practices in the following two articles. This can help avoid suspension due to the error "Received at from support address".

  • Forwarding incoming email from your existing email address to Zendesk Support
  • Managing your support addresses

Check your external email server authentication records setup to make sure inbound emails aren't classified as spam. See Understanding and configuring incoming email authentication (SPF, DKIM, DMARC, and ARC).

Ensure there's no unsupported multi-forwarding setup in place, or an email workflow that forwards one email through multiple locations before it reaches your Zendesk account.

Other resources to manage suspended tickets

  • Viewing, recovering, and deleting suspended tickets
  • Causes for ticket suspension
  • Guidelines for reviewing suspended tickets
  • Understanding suspended tickets and spam
  • Can I edit the suspended tickets view?
  • Error: Suspended ticket could not be recovered

articles.name: Announcing end of availability of Incremental APIs for third-party developers
articles.title: Announcing end of availability of Incremental APIs for third-party developers
articles.body:
Zendesk is announcing the end of availability of Incremental APIs for third-party developers. To protect sensitive customer data and strengthen ecosystem security as AI workflows scale, access to endpoints supporting bulk or incremental data transfers will be restricted for third parties. 

This announcement includes the following topics:

  • What is changing?
  • Why is Zendesk making this change?
  • What do I need to do?

What is changing?

To strengthen data security in the age of AI, Zendesk will no longer make Incremental APIs available to third-party developers. To minimize disruption, access will remain available for non-incremental and non-bulk transfer APIs.

These changes apply to all third-party apps and integrations that use the Zendesk APIs, whether or not they are listed on the Zendesk Marketplace.

The change will roll out in phases:

  • Rollout start: December 2, 2026
  • Rollout pause: December 17, 2026 – January 4, 2027
  • Completion target: January 19, 2027

Why is Zendesk making this change?

As companies rapidly adopt AI and automate critical workflows, APIs handle larger volumes of sensitive data. Incremental APIs are designed for bulk data transfer, which creates significant security risks if a third-party app’s credentials are ever compromised—allowing rapid exfiltration of large datasets.

Restricting third-party access to transactional and search APIs strengthens ecosystem security in two key ways:

  • Minimizes Exposure: Transactional APIs require a targeted approach, ensuring partners only request the specific records needed for their use case rather than pulling full timeframe datasets.

  • Limits Breach Impact: Non-incremental APIs prevent rapid bulk transfers, ensuring any unauthorized activity is contained to a smaller scale and detected much faster.

What do I need to do?

Zendesk Customers

  • Internal Use Cases: No action required. You may continue using Incremental APIs for internal integrations.

  • Third-Party Integrations: If a third-party app relies on an affected API, the developer must migrate to an approved endpoint to prevent service disruption.

  • Requesting an Extension: Starting November 2026, account admins can request a 60-day extension for partners:

  1. In Admin Center, select Apps & integrations > APIs > API Configuration.

  2. Select the partner(s) from the drop-down list and save the request.

Zendesk Partners

If your integration doesn't use Incremental APIs, you do not need to do anything.

If your integration uses Incremental APIs, you must migrate to alternative endpoints prior to enforcement.

If you have feedback or questions related to this announcement, visit our community forum where we collect and manage customer product feedback. For general assistance with your Zendesk products, contact Zendesk Customer Support.

articles.name: Error: ActionCollection declares more than one action
articles.title: Error: ActionCollection declares more than one action
articles.body:
Issue symptoms

I use AI agents and conversations saw an outage. In my conversation logs, I see this error: ActionCollection declares more than one action in environment. Cannot disambiguate at the tool layer.

Root cause

This error means that there are two actions with the same name, for example: User verification required. These two actions are called in the same Procedure. If you search, another Action exists with the same name.

Resolution steps

To resolve this issue:

  1. Rename one of the Actions so actions don't share the same name
  2. Update all references to the new Action name in your Procedures
  3. Publish any changes
  4. Test the result and correct your AI agents

articles.name: Voice AI agent pronunciation issues
articles.title: Voice AI agent pronunciation issues
articles.body:
Problem

A voice AI agent can occasionally have pronunciation issues. The AI agent might produce muffled, distorted, or otherwise unusual-sounding speech.

This is a rare known limitation that Zendesk cannot resolve during a live call. For background on how this issue is characterized, see the ElevenLabs documentation on corrupt speech. This resource provides information about the limitation, but does not provide a recovery step for a live call.

Solution

Use a default voice, such as Marin or Cedar, instead of a language-specific voice before deploying the AI agent. Voice selection is currently the most reliable mitigation.

Changes to models or voice settings might reduce how often the issue occurs, but they require extended testing to avoid overall regressions and aren't an immediate solution. There's no customer-side recovery path once the issue occurs during a live call.

If you report the issue to Zendesk Support, include the AI agent, selected voice, call date and time, call recording or conversation log, and the approximate time when the issue occurred. Zendesk will document updates as this known limitation is addressed.

articles.name: Release notes through 2026-09-18
articles.title: Release notes through 2026-09-18
articles.body:
See the What's New section for an overview of last month's releases.

This week's release notes include:

  • Admin Center
  • AI Agents
  • Copilot
  • Contact Center
  • Zendesk QA
  • Apps and integrations
  • Products with no updates this week

Admin Center

New:

  • The audit log events for creating and deleting OAuth tokens now show the OAuth client name in the Activity column

AI Agents

New:

  • Agentic email
    • As of September 16, 2026, all agentic email customers have access to new functionality for creating and using embedded templates in generative procedures, providing parity with the messaging channel.
  • Web crawler

    • Web crawler locale-handling updates are rolling out to better align crawled content with the locales configured for each help center.

      The rollout includes improved locale-filtering behavior and updated product guidance. See Understanding web crawler locales. The rollout is ongoing.

Fixed:

  • Agentic Email
    • Now completes the reply as expected when the AI agent's procedure finishes successfully.
    • Email turns that were failing to process now complete successfully.
  • Web Crawler
    • More reliable sitemap crawling. Fixed an issue that could prevent sitemap URLs from being discovered and crawled successfully. Web Crawler now handles sitemap depth separately from page-crawl depth, improving support for nested sitemaps.
    • Improved URL filtering. Web Crawler now filters start URLs marked as no-follow before fetching them. This reduces unnecessary requests and helps prevent unintended crawling.
    • Clearer crawler setup guidance. Improved the crawler creation experience with clearer start-URL labels and format guidance. Also fixed an untranslated example URL in localized crawler setup flows.
    • Improved error handling. Improved handling of product-limit connection errors so API clients receive more accurate error responses.

Copilot

New:

  • Similar tickets show agents past tickets that resemble the one they're working on, so they can apply proven solutions instead of starting from scratch. By reusing what already worked for that scenario, your agents can reduce average handling time and deliver faster, more consistent answers to customers. See Turning on similar tickets.

Contact Center

New:

Contact Center App

  • Upgraded Streams to 2.29.1 and ChatJS to 5.1.1 for improved stability across chat and voice calls.

Fixed:

Contact Center App

  • Improved onboarding for accounts using OAuth by enabling users to set the userId configuration field.
  • Fixed an issue where pressing Enter in the external search field caused the app to reload. 

Zendesk QA

New:

  • On September 21, 2026, we're updating the AI model for QA custom prompt evaluations. Review your prompts after this date to ensure outputs meet your expectations.
  • Restricted visibility of AutoQA score for Agents inside Zendesk QA
  • Zendesk QA HUB for easy QA set up and onboarding

Apps and integrations

New:
  • ZenTennis (Support)
    • ZenTennis gives support agents a playful break inside the Zendesk ticket sidebar. Agents play a first-to-five botanical rally, with configurable difficulty and keyboard, pointer, or on-screen controls. Administrators can optionally track completed results in the ticket.
  • Ticket Nibbler (Support)
    • Ticket Nibbler is a compact arcade-style break game in the ticket sidebar. Agents guide a growing worm around the board, eating plants while avoiding walls and its own body. It supports multiple control methods, configurable speed, and optional score tracking on tickets.
  • Refundid Returns and Exchanges (Support)
    • Refundid lets support agents see a customer's recent Refundid returns and refunds directly on the ticket, including references, order information, status, resolution, items, tracking, and shipping-label details. Agents can also search by order number or email and link into the Refundid merchant dashboard.
  • VendorApp Admin (Support)
    • VendorApp Admin embeds the VendorApp administration console inside Zendesk Support. It is designed for B2B2B and B2B2C support environments where vendors, partners, and customers need isolated branded portals while tickets, organizations, and users remain in Zendesk. The app provides in-Zendesk administration for portals, organizations, users, branding, and the Zendesk connection.
  • GrowOn Note Taker (Support)
    • GrowOn Note Taker lets agents create, edit, and delete ticket-specific working notes from the Zendesk sidebar without adding them to the ticket conversation. Notes remain associated with the ticket and retain creator and timestamp context. The app stores its note data in the customer's Zendesk account using Custom Objects.
  • SOCRadar Alert Management (Support)
    • SOCRadar Alert Management integrates SOCRadar's Extended Threat Intelligence platform with Zendesk Support. It can poll for new security alarms, create tickets automatically, display incidents in a dashboard, and let agents manage alarm status, severity, and comments from Zendesk. It supports multiple alarm categories including attack-surface, vulnerability, dark-web, brand-protection, fraud, threat-hunting, and supply-chain intelligence.
  • Refaire (Support)
    • Refaire is an AI-powered remote visual support platform that helps customers troubleshoot issues with their phone camera before human support is needed. When escalation occurs, it creates a Zendesk ticket containing diagnostic context such as attempted fixes, outcomes, product information, photos, and video. Agents can continue the support interaction in Zendesk and escalate according to configurable rules.
  • Data Custodian (Support) (paid)
    • Data Custodian lets you search the whole account with exact counts, export tickets with comments to CSV, Excel or JSON, change or delete thousands of tickets with undo, redact personal data, answer access requests with a complete pack, forget a person, run retention rules after a dry run. Every action leaves evidence.
  • Help Center Doctor (Support) (paid)

    • Help Center Doctor is a Zendesk app that scans and repairs help center content entirely within the customer’s browser. It checks articles and translations for issues such as broken links, missing alt text, stale or duplicate content, empty sections, and outdated translations. Key features include bulk fixes, find-and-replace, article editing, document exports, templates, snippets, and a link map. Changes are previewed, backed up locally, and reversible.

  • Help Center Article Templates (Support) (paid)

    • Help Center Article Templates helps Zendesk teams create help center articles without starting from scratch. It provides built-in templates for formats such as how-to guides, FAQs, troubleshooting articles, release notes, policies, product overviews, and announcements, along with reusable content snippets. Users can create custom templates, use fill-in placeholders, select sections, labels, languages, and permissions, and generate unpublished drafts directly in Zendesk. Pro users also get shared team libraries, multilingual drafts, publishing checklists, and JSON import/export.

  • Help Center Print & Export (Support) (paid)
    • Help Center Print & Export lets Zendesk users export any portion of their help center—individual articles, sections, categories, or the entire knowledge base—into professional documents without leaving Zendesk or using an external server. Users can filter and select content, choose a language, customize document formatting and branding, preview the results, and export them as PDFs, Word files, HTML, Markdown, ZIP folders, or CSV indexes. Export profiles and history make recurring documents and backups easy to repeat.
  • Help Center Find & Replace (Support) (paid)
    • Help Center Find & Replace lets Zendesk teams search and replace text, links, images, and HTML across all help center articles and languages. It supports plain-text and regular-expression searches, detailed filters, previews, diffs, and per-translation approval. Before making changes, it creates downloadable snapshots, reports progress and errors, and allows users to undo completed runs or restore snapshots. Saved searches simplify recurring rebrands and cleanups. The app also respects Zendesk permissions, warns about content blocks, and manages API requests within rate limits.
  • Help Center Link Checker (Support)
    • Help Center Link Checker scans every article and language to identify broken or problematic links and images. It detects missing, archived, draft, restricted, or outdated internal links, broken anchors, old-domain links, HTTP links, and external URLs or images that fail validation. It checks external resources through Zendesk’s proxy, distinguishes confirmed failures from unverified results, and provides a link map showing which articles reference a given article. Findings include explanations and direct links to the article editor, while repeat scans only recheck changed content.
  • Proactive Outreach (Support) (paid)
    • Proactive Outreach lets Zendesk Support teams send proactive messages to many customers by creating one ticket per recipient. It supports audiences built from users, organizations, matching tickets, or CSV files, with deduplication and extensive exclusions. Messages can use personalized placeholders, macros, previews, language variants, and customizable ticket settings. The app includes test tickets, opt-out handling, configurable delivery limits, pausing and resuming, retry support, and duplicate prevention. Campaign reports track delivery, failures, replies, and opt-outs, with ticket links and CSV export. Saved audiences, templates, and campaign history make recurring outreach easier.

Products with no updates this week

  • Knowledge
  • Voice
  • Analytics
  • Zendesk Workforce Management (WFM)
  • Mobile SDKs

articles.name: Error: AADSTS90015: Requested Query string is too long
articles.title: Error: AADSTS90015: Requested Query string is too long
articles.body:
Issue symptoms

Using SSO (Single Sign-On) and Microsoft, I see this error: AADSTS90015: Requested Query string is too long. How can I solve this?

Root cause

Input validation for a http listener has the limit of 4096 bytes and strings, which exceeds the AADSTS90015 limit. This is an issue on the Microsoft end, not from Zendesk.

Resolution steps

To overcome the issue:

  1. Clear your browser cookies, for example on Microsoft Edge and in Chrome
  2. For SAML (Security Assertion Markup Language), some applications send a long Relay State. However, SAML standard stipulate that the Relaystate value must not exceed 80 bytes in length. The permanent solution on the issue would be to ask the application vendor to shorten the request
Disclaimer: Zendesk provides this tutorial for instructional purposes only. Zendesk can't provide support for third-party technologies such as Microsoft. If the above article doesn't help, try searching for a solution online or contact Microsoft.

articles.name: Can I install multiple Web Widgets on the same web page?
articles.title: Can I install multiple Web Widgets on the same web page?
articles.body:
Question

Can I install multiple Web Widgets on the same web page?

Answer

No, installing more than one messaging Web Widget on the same exact page is not recommended by Zendesk. This poses several issues with storage and authentication.

Note: This recommendation applies to both the Web Widget (Classic) in live chat and the messaging Web Widget.

As a solution:

  • Only install a single Web Widget per web page
  • That widget can be live chat or messaging

articles.name: Why can SAML SSO create a duplicate end-user profile and remove an agent’s email address?
articles.title: Why can SAML SSO create a duplicate end-user profile and remove an agent’s email address?
articles.body:
Issue symptoms

Why does an agent who signs in through Security Assertion Markup Language (SAML) single sign-on (SSO) sometimes appear as a duplicate end user, while their corporate email address disappears from their original agent profile?

Root cause

This usually occurs when the SAML assertion does not consistently identify the intended Zendesk agent profile.

Zendesk uses the email address in the SAML subject’s NameID to identify users. The optional external_id attribute has special behavior: when it is included, Zendesk treats it as the user’s primary identifier. If the assertion sends an incorrect, missing, or inconsistent external_id, Zendesk can update or create an unintended user profile instead of associating the sign-in with the original licensed agent.

A new SSO profile defaults to an end-user role unless the SAML assertion explicitly provides a role. This can explain why the new profile cannot access agent functionality. In addition, Zendesk email identities must be unique. If the corporate email becomes associated with the unintended profile, it cannot remain on the original agent profile at the same time.

Resolution steps

To resolve the issue:

  1. Correct the identity-provider mapping before the affected agent signs in again. Verify that the NameID contains the correct corporate email and that any external_id is stable, unique, and consistently sent for that user. If external_id is not needed, consider omitting it rather than sending an unreliable value.
  2. Identify the original licensed agent profile and the duplicate end-user profile
  3. Correct or remove incorrect external IDs using the Users API, the SSO provider, or a bulk import. External IDs cannot be edited in the agent interface.
  4. Release the corporate email from the duplicate profile
  5. Restore and verify it on the original agent profile in Admin Center > People > Team > Team members
  6. If the duplicate profile has the corporate address as its primary email, add a temporary controlled email address, make it primary, and then remove the corporate address
  7. Do not merge the original agent and duplicate end-user profiles. Zendesk supports merging only between end-user accounts, and external IDs can introduce additional restrictions.
  8. After the identity mapping and email ownership are corrected, have the agent sign in again and confirm that Zendesk opens the intended agent profile with the expected role and access

articles.name: Configuring voicemail in Contact Center
articles.title: Configuring voicemail in Contact Center
articles.body:
Voicemail lets callers leave a message when they can't reach an agent. When a caller reaches a configured interactive voice response (IVR) path, Amazon Connect plays a greeting and records the message.

What's my plan?
Add-on Contact Center

Summary: ◀▼

Voicemail lets you capture caller messages when no agent is available, then create or link a ticket with the recording and optional transcript. You can assign the ticket to the right group, add tags and custom fields, and choose redacted or unredacted transcription. The article also covers setup, flow customization, testing, and troubleshooting missing recordings, transcripts, or duplicate tickets.

Voicemail lets callers leave a message when they can't reach an agent. When a caller reaches a configured interactive voice response (IVR) path, Amazon Connect plays a greeting and records the message.

Contact Center creates or links a Zendesk ticket with the voicemail details and recording. If transcription is enabled, Contact Center also adds the transcript to the ticket. Contact Center uses the Amazon Connect contact ID to match the recording and transcript to the ticket. The call record and recording can arrive in either order.

This article is for administrators who manage Zendesk Contact Center and Amazon Connect instances. It explains how to configure voicemail for each Amazon Connect queue, including ticket routing, tags, and transcription.

This article contains the following topics:

  • Preparing to configure voicemail
  • Configuring voicemail for a queue
  • Connecting voicemail to an inbound flow
  • Testing voicemail
  • Troubleshooting voicemail

Related articles:

  • Understanding how Contact Center calls become tickets
  • Mapping Amazon Connect attributes to Contact Center ticket fields

Preparing to configure voicemail

Before you configure voicemail, make sure that all of the following are true:

  • You have administrator access to Zendesk Contact Center and Amazon Connect.
  • Your Contact Center AWS CloudFormation stack version is 1.2.8 (20260908) or later. See Updating the Contact Center stack.
  • You have identified the Amazon Connect queues and inbound interactive voice response (IVR) paths that should offer voicemail.

Known limitation: When a voicemail caller doesn't match an existing end-user profile, Contact Center assigns the ticket requester to the Zendesk account owner instead of creating a new end-user profile for the caller. By default, the caller’s phone number appears in the ticket title. For more information, see Understanding how Contact Center calls become tickets.

Important: The Contact Center stack includes a managed contact flow named Zendesk Voicemail Template. Do not edit the managed flow. Copy it before you customize or connect it to an inbound path.

Configuring voicemail for a queue

Configure voicemail for every Amazon Connect queue that can transfer callers to your voicemail flow.

To configure voicemail for a queue

  1. In the Zendesk products menu, select Contact center.

  2. Under General, click Voicemail.

  3. Click Add voicemail configuration.

  4. Select the Amazon Connect Queue.

    This is the Amazon Connect queue associated with the voicemail path. Set this queue as the working queue in the inbound IVR before it transfers the caller to voicemail.

  5. Select the Zendesk Group that should receive new voicemail tickets.

    This setting applies only when voicemail creates a new ticket. It doesn't change a linked ticket's group, tags, or custom fields.

  6. Optional: Add ticket Tags.

    Zendesk adds the voicemail tag to new voicemail tickets automatically.

  7. Choose a Transcription mode, then click Save.

    Choose Disabled, Redacted, or Unredacted. Redacted transcription removes supported personally identifiable information (PII) from the transcript. Redaction is only available for English (en-US) and Spanish (es-US). Voicemails in any other language, including other English variants, are transcribed without redaction.

Connecting voicemail to an inbound flow

Use a copy of the managed voicemail template to collect the caller's message. Your inbound IVR controls when to offer voicemail. It transfers the caller to the copied flow.

To connect voicemail to an inbound flow

  1. In Amazon Connect, open Zendesk Voicemail Template.

  2. Click Save as and enter a meaningful name for the copied flow.

  3. In your inbound IVR, set the relevant Amazon Connect queue as the working queue before the caller enters the voicemail path.

  4. Transfer callers to the copied voicemail flow where you offer voicemail, such as after-hours, queue-unavailable, or error paths.

  5. Publish the updated inbound flow and associate it with the appropriate inbound number or routing path.

The template sets the contact attributes required to create the voicemail ticket. Preserve the attributes and their values when you customize the copied flow.

Customizing the voicemail flow

You can customize the greeting, recording prompt, closing message, error message, voice, language, and routing logic in your copied flow. Keep this recording sequence intact:

  1. Play the greeting and recording prompt.

  2. Enable recording for the customer, play the beep, and collect the caller's message.

  3. Disable recording before the closing message.

  4. Play the closing or error message, then disconnect the call.

Important: Do not remove or rename the voicemail attributes. Do not change the order of the recording steps. Otherwise, Contact Center might not identify the call as voicemail or attach the recording to the ticket.

Adding optional ticket attributes

Use contact attributes in the copied flow to add information to a new voicemail ticket:

  • custom_field_<Zendesk field ID>: Sets the named Zendesk ticket custom field. For example, custom_field_12345.
  • zendesk_ticket_id: Links the voicemail call to an existing Zendesk ticket. If the ticket ID is unavailable, Contact Center creates a new ticket.
Note: Preserve the queue name, queue Amazon Resource Name (ARN), caller number, and the template's required voicemail attribute. Contact Center needs these attributes to process the voicemail.

Testing voicemail

Test each IVR path that offers voicemail before you make it available to callers.

To test voicemail

  1. Call an inbound number and follow a voicemail path.

  2. Confirm that the expected greeting plays, leave a short message, and confirm that recording stops before the final message.

  3. In Amazon Connect, record the Contact Trace Record contact ID for the test call.

  4. In Zendesk, confirm that the expected ticket is created or updated. Confirm that it has the correct requester, group, tags, and custom fields.

  5. Confirm that the recording is attached and that the transcript matches the transcription setting.

Note: The call record and recording can arrive in either order. A short delay before the recording attachment appears on the ticket is expected.

Troubleshooting voicemail

Keep the Amazon Connect contact ID and call time for every voicemail issue. They help you trace the call across Amazon Connect and Zendesk.

This section contains the following topics:

  • Missing voicemail tickets
  • Missing voicemail recordings
  • Missing voicemail transcripts
  • Incorrect voicemail ticket values
  • Unexpected voicemail requesters
  • Duplicate voicemail tickets

Missing voicemail tickets

In the Amazon Connect Contact Trace Record, confirm all of the following:

  • The voicemail contact attribute is set to true.
  • The caller and dialed numbers are present.
  • The contact flow completed.

Also confirm that the Zendesk integration for the account is active. For information about how Contact Center creates or links tickets, see Understanding how Contact Center calls become tickets.

If a ticket isn't created, provide the contact ID and call time to your Contact Center deployment owner or Zendesk Customer Support. Don't place another test call until the issue is investigated.

Missing voicemail recordings

A short delay before a recording appears on the ticket is expected. If it doesn't appear, confirm that the WAV object exists in the account's recording bucket and that ZendeskRecordingEventsRule is enabled.

For instructions to enable the recording and transcript delivery triggers, see Setting up AWS to send call recordings to Zendesk Contact Center.

If the issue continues, use the contact ID to check the recording-ingest Lambda alarm and logs. Alternatively, provide the contact ID and call time to your Contact Center deployment owner or Zendesk Customer Support.

Missing voicemail transcripts

Confirm that transcription is enabled for the queue and that the caller's language supports the selected transcription mode. Then check the Amazon Transcribe job and its output object.

Confirm that ZendeskTranscriptEventsRule is enabled. For instructions to enable the recording and transcript delivery triggers, see Setting up AWS to send call recordings to Zendesk Contact Center.

If the issue continues, provide the contact ID and call time to your Contact Center deployment owner. They can investigate transcription, permissions, encryption, and EventBridge. The recording remains available even when transcription fails.

Incorrect voicemail ticket values

Review the voicemail configuration for the queue. Confirm that custom field attributes use the format custom_field_<numeric field ID>.

Group assignment and custom field values apply only when voicemail creates a new ticket. Correct the voicemail configuration or contact flow, then update any existing tickets using your normal Zendesk workflow.

For more information about contact attributes, see Mapping Amazon Connect attributes to Contact Center ticket fields.

Unexpected voicemail requesters

Check how many customer profiles match the caller's phone number. One match uses that profile. No match associates with the Zendesk account owner (by default the caller's phone number is added to the ticket title). When multiple profiles match, voicemail uses the first profile returned by the search.

You can't configure voicemail to use the caller's phone number as the requester when no profile, or multiple profiles, match. Create or consolidate customer profiles where reliable requester matching is needed.

Duplicate voicemail tickets

Compare the Amazon Connect contact IDs before you take corrective action. Provide the contact ID, ticket IDs, and timestamps to your Contact Center deployment owner or Zendesk Customer Support.

If the tickets have the same Amazon Connect contact ID and the account recently completed a dual-stack update, ask the deployment owner to check whether triggers for Lambda functions from the previous stack are still active. Triggers on the old Lambda functions must be turned off before triggers are enabled for the current stack. For more information, see Setting up AWS to send call recordings to Zendesk Contact Center (writeback).

Don't delete tickets or disable retries manually.
